core.title: Give every WMBT entry an id, a statement and its proving artifacts
core.given: A wagon decomposition containing What-Must-Be-True (WMBT) entries that you are authoring, editing, inspecting or validating.
core.when: You add, edit, review or validate any WMBT entry.
core.then: Every WMBT entry declares its id, its statement, and the proving artifacts (the acceptances/tests that prove the statement).
prefer: Write the id, the statement and the list of proving acceptances/tests together when the entry is created.
When reviewing existing entries, flag or complete any entry lacking id, statement or proving artifacts.
avoid: A WMBT entry missing its id, its statement, or its proving artifacts.
Listing proving artifacts that do not actually prove the entry's statement.
core.why: Downstream planning (per-WMBT acceptance coverage, feature grouping, smoke acceptances) operates over enumerated, well-shaped WMBTs; an entry without id, statement or proof cannot be referenced or verified.
evidence: Each WMBT entry in the wagon decomposition has a non-empty id, a non-empty statement and at least one referenced proving artifact (acceptance/test).
verification: Severity 2, disposition documentation-only: verified by reading the wagon decomposition; this rule preserves no automated detector.
Check vocabulary: a wmbt_entry is a What-Must-Be-True entry in a wagon decomposition; proving_artifacts are the acceptances/tests that prove the WMBT statement.

Scope: the check establishes presence — a non-empty id, a non-empty statement and at least one referenced proving artifact per entry; whether a referenced artifact genuinely proves the statement is a review judgment covered by the avoid guidance, not a separate mechanical check.

fires: The planner adds a new WMBT entry to a wagon decomposition.
The planner edits any field of an existing WMBT entry.
The planner inspects, reviews or validates existing WMBT entries in a wagon decomposition, even without editing them.
The planner restructures or regenerates a wagon decomposition that contains WMBT entries.
doesNotFire: Work that neither authors, inspects nor validates WMBT entries (e.g. editing unrelated planning documents).
Implementing code or tests for an already-shaped WMBT (coder work, not planning).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan_artifact role and hold a wagon decomposition or WMBT entries, so the file_kind activation fact can be evaluated in a given stack.

bunOnly.text: parity.implementation_preserved=false — a reference to the frozen ATDD-Bun sidecar's parity bookkeeping field.
bunOnly.reason: The sidecar's parity flags are bookkeeping of the Bun realization; the neutral core keeps only the rule-level severity, the documentation-only disposition and the absence of an automated detector.

classification.note: Method-level situation; names no stack, runtime, path or suffix.
Neutral trigger over WMBT entry work.
Single obligation over the shape of a WMBT entry; kept verbatim, no conditions added or dropped.
Role-level authoring move; no stack specifics.
Role-level review move; no stack specifics.
Neutral: proving artifacts must actually prove the entry's statement.
Neutral presence check over the entries of a wagon decomposition.
Per-rule severity and disposition are rule-level verification, not profile keys; mapped to the core verification entry on severity/disposition and review-by-reading.
Term definitions are method-level; carried as check vocabulary in the core's verification array.
Severity, documentation-only disposition and absence of a detector go to core verification; the parity.implementation_preserved field reference is Bun sidecar bookkeeping.
wagon and wmbt are method artifact names (also in the urn vocabulary's artifact params); the concrete file kinds that hold them in a given stack come from the profile.
Logical change kinds over WMBT entries; stack-neutral, needs a diff-level observer.
Neutral planning phases; judged from the task.

neutralityNotes: The convention is method-level (WMBT entries inside a wagon decomposition) and needed almost no neutralization; WMBT and wagon are ATDD-method artifact names — also artifact params in the closed urn vocabulary — so they remain in the core. The only realization-specific content is the sidecar parity reference in verifier_detail[1]. Which concrete file kinds hold wagon decompositions / WMBT entries is per-stack and is supplied through roles.plan_artifact.kinds; the id's concrete shape is left to each realization because bun.json states no value for it.
